summary: ```markdown # CLO Technique Workshop - Custom Texture Outline ## Introduction In this workshop, we will explore the process of creating a custom texture outline using the CLO technique. The following steps outline the necessary actions to achieve the desired texture effects. ## Opening the Texture First, open the well-treated famous line texture. The texture in the picture is continuously transparent. ## Image and Unit Settings - **Image Size**: Ensure the unit size is changed to inches. - **Length Determination**: The length of the famous line is determined by the SPI value. SPI stands for "Samples Per Inch," indicating how many frames are present in one inch. - **Width and Height Settings**: You can set the width of the picture to the corresponding number of inches. At the same time, pay attention to the height of the picture. ## Saving the Image After adjusting the settings: 1. Save the PNG picture. 2. Click "Save." If you do not need to save, click "Cancel." ## Creating a New Famous Line Next, navigate to the software to create a newly built famous line. 1. Switch to the well-treated famous line. 2. Skip some value settings initially. 3. Add the well-treated picture. ## Adjusting Width and SPI - Since the width of the picture is 0.5 inches, there will be two frames in one inch. - Choose SPIR (Samples Per Inch Ratio). - Switch to the thin unit of the line, which should be 8.89 mm. This value will affect the well-treated settings. ## Value Input and Free Famous Line - Input a value as needed. - Use the free famous line feature to add the famous line to the board. ## 3D Window Adjustments - Enlarge the details in the 3D window. - If you want the famous line to be cut with the board, set the value of the well-treated to half the height of the famous line. ## Overall Effect and Image Generation - Review the overall effect of the adjustments made. - Use the auto-generated PBR sticker to generate the well-treated image. - Click to generate the well-treated image and then click the browse button. ## Final Adjustments - Note that the well-treated image may appear upside down; make sure to turn it off if needed. - Adjust the well-treated strength to negative to enhance the effect. - Enlarge the famous line to check for any inconsistencies, such as small cracks between the well-treated picture. ## Conclusion Finally, switch to the well-treated image to display the very well-treated image. Now the famous line is cut, achieving the desired outcome. ```
